title: Best Hill Stations in India in Winter: Snow, Sunshine and Clear Views
seoTitle: Best Hill Stations in India in Winter: Snow and Sunshine
metaDescription: The best hill stations in India for winter: snowy Gulmarg, Manali and Auli, clear-view Kumaon and Darjeeling, and mild southern hills such as Munnar, Ooty and Coorg.
description: A guide to the best hill stations in India in winter, December to February: snow resorts such as Gulmarg, Manali, Auli and Narkanda, clear-view hills such as Kausani, Mukteshwar and Darjeeling, and the mild southern hills of Munnar, Ooty, Kodaikanal and Coorg, with cold-weather tips and Christmas and New Year planning.
dek: Winter splits India's hills in two: snowbound Himalayan resorts, and sunny, mild southern hills. Both have their appeal.

hero.alt: Snow on the trees and Christ Church in Shimla

intro: From December to February, Himalayan hill stations are cold and, at higher places, often snowy, while the southern and western hills are at their mildest and clearest. Winter is also when the Himalaya is most visible, with crisp air and long views.
Christmas and New Year bring a second peak season to Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie and the southern hills, so plan early for those dates.
quickAnswer: The best hill stations in winter in India are Gulmarg, Manali, Auli, Kufri and Narkanda for snow; Kausani, Mukteshwar, Darjeeling and Pelling for clear Himalayan views; and Munnar, Ooty, Kodaikanal, Coorg and Mahabaleshwar for mild, sunny days. Snow is most likely from late December to February but never guaranteed; carry proper warm clothing and check road conditions.
takeaways: December to February is cold in the Himalaya and pleasant in the southern and western hills.
Snow is likeliest in Gulmarg, Manali (Solang), Auli, Narkanda and Kufri in mid-winter.
The clearest Himalayan views of the year come in winter.
Christmas and New Year are very busy in Shimla, Manali and Mussoorie.
Heavy snowfall can close roads for a day or more; keep buffer days.

sections.heading: Christmas and New Year
paras: The last week of December is one of the busiest of the year in Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, Nainital and the southern hills. Book stays and transport well ahead, expect higher rates and traffic, and plan New Year's Eve close to where you are staying. If you want snow for Christmas, remember it is never certain that early in the season; January and February are more reliable.

sections.heading: Staying warm and safe
list: Pack thermals, a down or insulated jacket, gloves, a cap and warm socks.
Ask stays about room heating and hot water before booking.
Roads can freeze in the morning; hire drivers experienced with snow and ice.
Carry snacks and water in the car in case of delays.

sections.heading: Quieter winter choices
paras: If you want winter light without the holiday crowds, look at Kumaon villages such as Binsar and Mukteshwar, Kalimpong instead of Darjeeling, Chail or Narkanda instead of Shimla, and Coonoor, Kotagiri or Vagamon in the south. Weekdays in January are the calmest time almost everywhere.

sections.heading: Winter combinations
list: Shimla with Narkanda or Kufri for a chance of snow.
Manali with Solang and Sissu through the Atal Tunnel.
Srinagar with Gulmarg for snow and skiing.
Munnar with Thekkady and the Alappuzha backwaters in the south.

sections.heading: Winter food
paras: Winter is the season for warming mountain food: thukpa and momos in Darjeeling, Sikkim and Himachal, Kashmiri kahwa and harissa in Srinagar, siddu in Himachal, and hot chai at every roadside stop. In the south, winter brings plantation crops such as coffee and pepper to harvest.

safety: Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road and weather updates, and avoid driving after dark.
Snowfall varies from year to year and is never guaranteed; watch forecasts and keep your dates flexible.
Permits, e-passes, ropeways and pass openings change; check official portals before you travel.
Use heaters safely; never burn coal or charcoal in a closed room.

faqs.q: Which hill station is best in winter?
faqs.a: Gulmarg, Manali and Auli for snow; Kausani and Darjeeling for views; Munnar, Ooty and Coorg for mild weather.

faqs.q: Which hill stations have snow in December?
faqs.a: Gulmarg and higher parts of Manali and Auli often do by late December, but snow is not guaranteed that early.

faqs.q: Is it too cold to visit the Himalaya in winter?
faqs.a: It is cold but manageable with proper clothing and heated stays; very high places are harsh.

faqs.q: Which hill stations are good for Christmas and New Year?
faqs.a: Shimla, Manali, Mussoorie, Nainital, Munnar and Ooty are popular; book early.

faqs.q: Are southern hill stations cold in winter?
faqs.a: Nights can be chilly, especially in Ooty and Kodaikanal, but days are usually mild and sunny.
